column2: The ice has not broken on the bay, and the stores are down to salt fish and hard bread. Two families have already come to blows over a shared cache. The village headman wants you to decide who eats and who waits.
Organize a fair distribution.
Hold a public gathering and encourage generosity.

The young firebenders have built a ring of stone in the market square and hung it with red cloth. They want to perform for the town. The captain of the watch has posted guards with buckets of sand, and the merchants have moved their stalls back.
Make the exhibition disciplined and instructive.
Fund a grand display worthy of the nation.

A delegation from the rice villages has brought a cracked clay tablet with forty names pressed into it. The eastern canal has silted up, and the road to the market is little more than a cart track. The headman says the last magistrate promised to fix both before the flood season.
Send officials to assess the problem.
Hear the petition publicly and win the villagers' trust.

The temple's evening bell has rung twice, but no one has gone to supper. Two travelling monks are arguing about whether the old texts should be copied for outsiders or kept behind the temple wall. The abbot has saved you a cushion between them.
Listen carefully and study their arguments.
Encourage them to share their wisdom beyond the temple.

The spring run has brought the fishing boats together in the same narrow channel. The northern village says the southern boats are setting nets across the spawning beds. The southern headman says his people have fished those beds since before the northern village had a name.
Set clear seasonal limits.
Ask the elders to mediate according to tradition.

Two officers in the local garrison have stopped speaking to each other. One says the other sold the regiment's coal to a merchant. The other says the first has been drilling his men on the parade ground after dark, without orders. The soldiers have begun to take sides.
Settle the matter through a strict review of duties.
Call for a public oath of service and unity.

A merchant caravan has come in with two empty wagons and a driver who will not stop shaking. The bandits took the silk and left the iron, which means they knew what the caravan carried and when it would pass. The traders want a patrol. Your steward wants to know who will pay for it.
Organize patrols and repair the road.
Invite merchants to fund a joint watch.

Three travelling monks arrive at the temple gate on foot, their robes grey with road dust. One has a fever and the other two will not leave him. The temple's storekeeper says there is room in the guest hall, but the winter stores are already counted.
Offer them lodging and time for study.
Help them on their way and ask them to carry your good wishes.

The thaw came early, and the ice paths along the eastern shore have opened in three places. A hunter lost a sled and two dogs in the black water. The old guides want to mark a longer route over the glacier. The younger hunters want to bridge the gaps with planks and rope.
Coordinate repairs with the local guides.
Hold a gathering to share knowledge of safe travel.

The shipwright has brought a model of a new hull to court. It is wider than the old patrol boats and sits lower in the water. She says it will carry more grain and fewer oars. The admiral says it will look like a merchant's barge at a time when the ports need to see a warship.
Prioritize reliable ships and skilled crews.
Sponsor a grand launch to raise morale.

A farmer's widow says the magistrate awarded her neighbor's field to a merchant who paid in silver. The clerk's ledger has a second set of numbers in the margin. The magistrate is a cousin of the district's richest landholder, and the district has been quiet for years.
Order a careful and impartial review.
Hear both sides openly before the community.

The young monks have asked for a week of silence in the high pasture. The temple's elders say the roofs need mending and the goats need bringing down before the snow. The young ones say they have been mending and bringing all summer, and that the wind has stopped speaking to them.
Give them time to reflect and learn.
Ask them to combine their practice with service to others.
